A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SEED research work. All 20 pages, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–E, support reliable comparison; content displaced by text reflow can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original human-rating studies, comparisons of evaluation metrics, robustness analyses, and re-evaluation of five decoding models in Sections 5 and appendices B–E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including human-alignment measurements in Tables 1–5 and decoding-model evaluations in Table 6.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same Object F1 computation, caption-based Cap-Sim, EfficientNet correlation, and equal-weight averaging into SEED. No algorithm, component, or computation changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same NSD and GOD image reconstructions, semantic and perceptual human-rating tasks, and decoding models. No dataset, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same eight conventional metric comparators. Table 5 retains the same component combinations and BLIP/GIT VQA comparisons, and Table 6 retains the same five decoding models.

E3.justification: Both retain 1,000 NSD pairs with 22 evaluators, the same four-subject sampling scheme, and 50 GOD reconstructions with 10 evaluators. Rating scales, meta-evaluation metrics, model configurations, and failure-mode thresholds are unchanged.

E4.justification: The component substitutions, VLM-generated category experiment, size/location/count ablations, metric-combination analysis, and worst-case examples are retained in Section 5 and appendices B–D. The questions tested and supporting evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 retains 1,000 evaluator-axis bootstrap iterations and the same 95% confidence intervals for SEED–EffNet differences. Inter-rater agreement statistics and other uncertainty-reporting practices also remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and qualitative findings match across Tables 1–6 and the figures. For example, SEED retains 81.0% pairwise accuracy, .621 Kendall correlation, and .813 Pearson correlation on NSD, and 73.7%, .477, and .706 on GOD.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), threshold-cutoff reasoning, relaxed object recall, and failure-mode criteria are unchanged. Equation spacing and relocation do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: SEED's complementary metrics, stronger alignment with human judgments, identification of decoding failures, and release of human-evaluation data.

C2.justification: Interpretations of component errors, semantic near-misses, missing semantic details, and potential remedies are unchanged. Section 6 and Appendix D retain the same limitations concerning inherited model errors, distorted images, and perceptual fidelity.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same component models, object-category lists, threshold increments, survey procedures, compensation, and evaluation details. The stated code and human-evaluation data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 deletes a duplicated NeuroPictor description in Section 2.1, but the same description and Huo et al. citation remain earlier in that section. The cited-work coverage, bibliography, and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 removes one repeated sentence about NeuroPictor fine-tuning its diffusion model and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose and section organization are unchanged apart from reflow.

P2.justification: Text reflow shifts equations, tables, and figures within the main text: Equation (4) moves from page 6 to page 5, and Tables 1–2 move upward on page 7. Figure content, captions, and table structures remain unchanged; appendix pages render identically.

improvement.justification: Removing the duplicated NeuroPictor sentence slightly reduces redundancy, but the remaining changes are presentation shifts and the updated arXiv stamp. The method, empirical support, reproducibility information, limitations, and appendices are unchanged, yielding no meaningful paper-level quality difference.
